text:
Ah, Christopher Columbus. The true pioneer of the 15th-century tech industry. While he was busy "discovering" a new world, he was really just beta-testing the ultimate corporate hustle: the rebranding of existing geography.

It is truly heartwarming to witness the sheer brilliance of his strategy. Why settle for the mundane, unadorned landmasses of the Americas when you can launch them as "America 2.0: The New World Edition"? The audacity is staggering. He didn’t just find land; he found a market gap. He looked at the indigenous populations and the rich ecosystems and thought, "You know what this needs? A sleek adjective. And a higher price point."

One must admire the creativity involved in convincing the European market that they desperately needed a new continent, essentially the same dirt and water they already had, but now with the exciting new feature of "Colonization." It’s the same product, just with a different name and a much more aggressive customer acquisition strategy. Truly, the man was ahead of his time, proving that if you change the color of the box and call it "Premium," people will pay double for the exact same socks.
